annotations.keyFindings: In 2,140 resections in 11 hospitals, full compliance (38 percent) was associated with fewer infections (9.8 against 16.1 percent; adjusted odds ratio 0.61).
annotations.limitations: Unblinded compliance recording; few emergency cases.

annotations.keyFindings: Oral antibiotic bowel preparation was associated with lower infection (odds ratio 0.52); glove change showed no clear association; elements were strongly correlated.
annotations.limitations: Elective cases only; compliance from operation notes.

annotations.keyFindings: Across 24 studies, bundles were associated with lower infection (risk ratio 0.56); only 5 studies included post-discharge surveillance.
Forty-seven percent of infections were diagnosed after discharge; a day-30 phone call found 83 percent of post-discharge infections.
annotations.limitations: Three hospitals; unreachable patients older and living alone.

annotations.keyFindings: Counting non-applicable elements as delivered inflated emergency-case compliance from 31 to 44 percent; an all-or-none score over applicable elements was stable and quick.
In 1,030 emergency resections, infection was 21 percent; contamination and stoma formation were the strongest predictors; full compliance only 19 percent.
End-of-surgery temperature below 36.0 degrees in 18 percent; no glucose measurement in 41 percent of patients without diabetes.

claims.text: In 2,140 colorectal resections across 11 hospitals, full bundle compliance was associated with fewer surgical site infections (9.8 against 16.1 percent; adjusted odds ratio 0.61).
claims.passage: Surgical site infection occurred in 9.8 percent of fully compliant cases and 16.1 percent of others (adjusted odds ratio 0.61, 95 percent CI 0.46 to 0.81).
claims.interpretation: An association worth estimating locally; the planning value for the sample size.

claims.text: Of 412 surgical site infections after colorectal resection, 47 percent were diagnosed after discharge, and a day-30 phone call detected 83 percent of post-discharge infections.
claims.passage: Of 412 surgical site infections detected after colorectal resection in three hospitals, 47 percent were diagnosed after discharge.
claims.interpretation: The existing day-30 call is essential and must reach patients who live alone.

claims.text: Counting non-applicable elements as delivered inflated full compliance in emergency cases from 31 to 44 percent.
claims.passage: Counting non-applicable elements as delivered inflated full compliance in emergency cases from 31 to 44 percent
claims.interpretation: Use an all-or-none score over applicable elements with written applicability rules.

claims.text: In 1,030 emergency colorectal resections, infection occurred in 21 percent and full bundle compliance was recorded in only 19 percent.
claims.passage: Full bundle compliance was recorded in only 19 percent of emergency cases
claims.interpretation: Emergency status confounds the compliance-infection association and must be adjusted for.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. A multicentre prospective study associated full bundle compliance with fewer infections (adjusted odds ratio 0.61), and a meta-analysis of mostly before-and-after studies agrees, while element-level estimates are unstable because elements are correlated. Almost half of infections appear after discharge, and a day-30 call finds most of them. Compliance must be scored over applicable elements, and emergency surgery, with low compliance and high infection, confounds the comparison. Three model leads remain unverified.
gradeRationale: Observational and before-and-after evidence with confounding by emergency status and unblinded compliance recording; consistent direction, low certainty for a causal effect.
summary: Seven records appraised; four claims; one out-of-range score refused.
